findings.snippet:
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "app" {
  name                = "app-asg"
  min_size            = 6
  max_size            = 6
  desired_capacity    = 6
  vpc_zone_identifier = ["subnet-abc"]
}
findings.message: This Auto Scaling Group's min_size equals its max_size (6), so it can never scale down — it runs 6 instances around the clock regardless of load. Set a lower min_size (or a floor tied to real traffic) so idle capacity isn't billed, and emitting carbon, 24/7.

This S3 bucket has no lifecycle rule, so objects accumulate (and keep being billed and re-replicated) forever. Add a lifecycle_rule (or a separate aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration) to expire or transition old objects to a cheaper, lower-carbon storage class.

This EC2 instance uses a large/xlarge-class instance type (m5.4xlarge). Oversized instances amplify both cost and carbon footprint when the workload doesn't need that much capacity; right-size against real CPU/memory utilization, or move variable load onto an Auto Scaling Group instead of a fixed large size.
